title: Maaya Rajeshwaran, 17, Wins First Pro Title and Breaks Sania Mirza's 22-Year Record
excerpt: The Coimbatore teenager swept the singles and doubles at the W35 Lagos event in Portugal, beating the top seed from 0-5 down — and becoming the youngest Indian woman to win a W35 singles crown.
body:
• Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi, 17, won her first professional singles title at the ITF W35 tournament in Lagos, Portugal, beating Spain's Celia Cerviño Ruiz 6-4, 6-2 in the final.
  • At 17 years and three months, she became the youngest Indian woman to win a W35 singles title — breaking a record Sania Mirza set at 17 years and 10 months in Lagos, Nigeria, in 2004.
  • Ranked around world No. 1,038 before the week, she came through qualifying, beat top seed Justina Mikulskyte after trailing 0-5 in the first set, and did not drop a set in the main draw.
  • She also won the doubles title with Ukraine's Yelyzaveta Kotliar — a double crown months after leaving the Rafael Nadal Academy to transition to the senior circuit.

Indian teenager Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi has won her first professional title, and she did it in a place with a familiar name in Indian tennis history. The 17-year-old from Coimbatore swept the singles and doubles crowns at the ITF W35 tournament in Lagos, Portugal, beating Spain's Celia Cerviño Ruiz 6-4, 6-2 in the singles final without dropping a set in the main draw. The win makes her the youngest Indian woman to capture a W35 singles title — breaking a record Sania Mirza had held for 22 years, since winning in Lagos, Nigeria, in 2004 at 17 years and 10 months. Maaya was 17 years and three months.

"I don't think you can actually surpass her, because she's a legend and she'll always remain a legend."

— Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi, on Sania Mirza

A qualifier's run

The ranking told none of the story. Maaya arrived ranked around No. 1,038 and had to qualify for the main draw. Her first-round opponent was the top seed, Justina Mikulskyte, ranked No. 246 — and Maaya fell behind 0-5 in the opening set. She has described glancing at the courtside clock, deciding she was not losing a set in 25 minutes, and clawing the set back before closing the match in straight sets. She then beat Argentina's Berta Bonardi 6-2, 6-0 and eighth seed Tian Jialin 6-2, 6-1 on her way to the final, and partnered Ukraine's Yelyzaveta Kotliar to the doubles title for a double crown.

The Nadal Academy chapter

The title is also a transition marker. Maaya trained at the Rafael Nadal Academy before leaving a few months ago to commit to the senior circuit — a step up she has said has been demanding. Her Lagos week is the first hard evidence the transition is working: wins over the top seed and a string of higher-ranked opponents, closed out with a straight-sets final.

What it means for Indian tennis

Maaya was quick to wave off the Mirza comparison, telling IANS she still looks up to her idol through interviews and podcasts and hopes to learn from her. The record, though, is the record: no Indian woman had won at this level this young in more than two decades. The next test is repetition — stacking results at W35 and higher events to turn a breakthrough week into a ranking that earns direct entry, rather than qualifying rounds, at bigger tournaments.

What's next

Maaya has said she plans more professional tournaments as she builds her senior schedule. Her updated ranking after Lagos will decide how ambitious that schedule can be — and whether Indian tennis's newest name starts appearing in the draws that matter by the new season.
